correctness.rationale: Any proper ideal lies in J and is an F-linear subspace because J²=0, so there are S+1 ideals including R. A nonzero ordered product arises exactly when all entries are R or one entry is nonzero proper and others R, yielding 1+k(S−1) cases. Elementary comparison with field and Gaussian subspace counts gives unique (2,2,2) equality. F2[x,y]/(x,y)² has 6 ideals with 27 zero pairs; classifying order4 and order6 commutative unital nonfields proves order8 minimality. Independent subspace/ideal counting and field comparisons verify examples; symbolic proof is all q,d,k.

originality.rationale: The named 2026 paper introduces zeta_k and conjectures only fields have zeta_k equal to field value. Its inspected Conjecture 4.2 and Section 10 explicitly leave nonprincipal short-local cases open. Its chain/principal computations do not cover d=2 square-zero local rings with nonprincipal maximal ideal. Prior element-zero-product probabilities are a distinct sampling model; no Resultary hit gives this counterexample.
residual_risks: The collision uniqueness is only for square-zero local nonfields; other finite rings may collide at k>=2.
The classification of all order-eight equality examples is not asserted.
